is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae sensu lato, specifically An. coluzzii and An. gambiae sensu stricto (page 1, 3, 5).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for L1014F vgsc-kdr and G119S-ace-1 (page 3, 5, 8, 9).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Tables 1 and 2 provide genotype counts (RR, RS, SS) for L1014F and G119S-ace-1 across different study arms and time points (pages 8 and 9).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in the field in the CoZO health zone, Zou department, Southern Benin (page 2, 3).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is a primary empirical study evaluating the impact of LLINs on the genetic structure of mosquito populations (page 2).

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in the CoZO health zone (Cove-Ouinhi-Zagnanado), Zou department, Benin (page 2, 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections occurred between September 2019 and October 2021 (page 3).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study is a new analysis of samples collected during a specific RCT (Accrombessi et al. 2021, 2023). While the samples are part of a larger trial, this paper presents original genetic analysis not previously published.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and allele frequencies are provided in the main text tables (Tables 1 and 2).

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the impact of dual-active ingredient LLINs (pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr and pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen) on the genetic structure of Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations in Southern Benin. Genotyping for L1014F vgsc-kdr and G119S-ace-1 was performed on field-collected mosquitoes over a two-year period post-intervention. The study found high frequencies of the L1014F resistance allele and low frequencies of the G119S-ace-1 allele, with no significant changes in allele frequencies attributable to the new net types.
